question: None shared. P-158's compared figure (95% accuracy) separates Alzheimer's dementia from cognitively normal speakers on ADReSS (Pitt Cookie Theft recordings). P-58's figures separate MCI from healthy controls (Petersen criteria) using 'describe your previous day' monologues recorded in New York and Szeged. The positive label covers a different population class: AD dementia in one, MCI in the other. P-158's second dataset (MUDC, 60 Turkish clinic patients) is described both as 'patients with mild cognitive impairment' and as 'cognitively normal (CN) and AD patients', and its classification label is never defined as MCI against healthy controls. No P-158 figure therefore addresses P-58's question. The broad channel (speech) is shared. The features differ (spectral/MFCC acoustic features against ASR-derived temporal and pause parameters), which condition 1 would allow.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy, a nominal match. The record's P-58 value '67-92%' is a span across accuracy, precision, recall, specificity and F1 over feature subsets and ASR languages, not a single accuracy. P-58's monolingual full-feature accuracies are 84.8% (English) and 75.8% (Hungarian), both taken at the equal error rate.

figures.P-158: ADReSS AD vs non-AD, random forest, 10-fold CV over speed-perturbed 20-second segments (1520 training samples from 153 recordings): 95% (+/- 0.07). Segments of one recording are not independent, so no subject-level interval can be derived for this figure. ADReSS held-out test set: 73% for 'dementia or not'. The test-set size is printed both as 48 and as 60 recordings. Wilson 95% CI at n=48: [0.591, 0.835]; at n=60: [0.606, 0.826]. MUDC MLP 94% on an undefined label (Wilson at n=60, ignoring augmentation: [0.850, 0.978]).

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-158 reports no MCI-against-healthy-control result, and P-58 reports no dementia result. On P-158's only subject-level figure (held-out 73%), P-58's English and Hungarian Wilson intervals ([0.691, 0.934] and [0.590, 0.872]) both contain 0.73. P-58's 84.8% lies just outside P-158's held-out interval ([0.606, 0.826] at n=60), so the evidence on uncertainty is mixed. The 95% headline is a segment-level cross-validated figure computed on augmented segments of the same recordings.
performance_validity: The formal exclusion does not apply: 95% is below 0.97. P-158's 95% is a weak estimate, however. It comes from cross-validation over segments cut from the same recordings and speed-perturbed, which lets one speaker's segments fall in both training and test folds, and P-158's own held-out test accuracy is 73%. P-58 uses speaker-wise nested leave-one-out CV on 33 speakers per language.
reason: The two papers do not share a clinical question. P-158's 95% separates Alzheimer's dementia from cognitively normal speakers, P-58 separates MCI from healthy controls, and P-158 defines no MCI-against-control label on its Turkish data (condition 1). The record also treats P-58's '67-92%' span of several metrics as one accuracy estimate and computes the 0.28 gap from its lower end (condition 6). On the only subject-level P-158 figure (73%), P-58's own intervals contain it.
